name: audio/dls
description:
DLS (Downloadable Sounds) is a format for shipping the instrument samples a MIDI (Musical Instrument Digital Interface) sequence expects. The MIDI Manufacturers Association defined it, and RFC 4613 registers the media type. Without it, a score is left to whatever synthesiser the playback device happens to have.

A DLS file holds wavetable samples together with the articulation data that maps them across the keyboard. Bundling one with a sequence for handsets is what [audio/mobile-xmf](/audio/mobile-xmf) does.

furtherReading.title: RFC 4613 - Media Type Registrations for Downloadable Sounds for Musical Instrument Digital Interface (MIDI)

name: audio/mobile-xmf
description:
Mobile XMF is a profile of the Extensible Music Format aimed at handsets, registered by RFC 4723. XMF packages a MIDI (Musical Instrument Digital Interface) sequence together with the DLS (Downloadable Sounds) instrument bank it expects into one file. A ringtone therefore sounds the same everywhere, instead of depending on each device's built-in synthesiser.

That bundling is what the format exists for. The two parts it contains are [audio/midi](/audio/midi) and [audio/dls](/audio/dls).

furtherReading.title: RFC 4723 - Registration of Media Type audio/mobile-xmf

name: audio/sp-midi
description:
Scalable Polyphony MIDI constrains General MIDI so a sequence degrades predictably on a device that cannot sound every voice at once. The composer marks which notes matter most. A synthesiser short of polyphony then drops the others in a defined order rather than an arbitrary one.

It was written for mobile phones, and the MIDI Manufacturers Association specifies it as Recommended Practice RP-034, published December 2001. It shares the `.mid` extension with ordinary [audio/midi](/audio/midi).

name: audio/evrc
description:
EVRC (Enhanced Variable Rate Codec) is the speech codec 3GPP2 standardised as C.S0014 for CDMA (Code Division Multiple Access) networks. It picks a rate frame by frame between full, half and eighth rate. Speech gets the full rate and silence almost no bits at all, which is how CDMA networks fitted more calls onto one carrier.

RFC 4788 registers the storage format for the EVRC family. Its later members are [audio/evrcb](/audio/evrcb), [audio/evrcwb](/audio/evrcwb) and [audio/evrcnw](/audio/evrcnw).

IANA spells this type `audio/EVRC`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 4788 - Enhancements to RTP Payload Formats for EVRC Family Codecs

name: audio/evrc-qcp
description:
This is EVRC speech stored in QCP, the RIFF-based file format Qualcomm defined for vocoder data. RFC 3625 registers QCP together with the media types for the codecs carried inside it.

QCP is how CDMA (Code Division Multiple Access) handsets saved voice memos, and how vocoder test vectors were exchanged. The bare storage format without the wrapper is [audio/evrc](/audio/evrc), and the same wrapper around the Selectable Mode Vocoder is [audio/smv-qcp](/audio/smv-qcp).

IANA spells this type `audio/EVRC-QCP`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 3625 - The QCP File Format and Media Types for Speech Data

name: audio/evrcb
description:
EVRC-B is the second generation of the CDMA (Code Division Multiple Access) Enhanced Variable Rate Codec, standardised by 3GPP2 as C.S0014-B. It keeps the variable-rate structure of the original. What it adds is finer control over the average rate, so an operator can balance capacity against voice quality across a wider range.

RFC 5188 registers this media type alongside the wideband [audio/evrcwb](/audio/evrcwb). The narrowband original is [audio/evrc](/audio/evrc).

IANA spells this type `audio/EVRCB`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 5188 - RTP Payload Format for the Enhanced Variable Rate Wideband Codec (EVRC-WB) and the Media Subtype Updates for EVRC-B Codec

name: audio/evrcnw
description:
EVRC-NW is the narrowband-wideband member of the CDMA (Code Division Multiple Access) EVRC family from 3GPP2. One stream can carry narrowband or wideband frames and switch between them mid-call. A handset moving through changing coverage therefore degrades smoothly, instead of the call being switched to a different codec.

RFC 6884 defines its RTP payload format and registers this media type. It follows [audio/evrcb](/audio/evrcb) and [audio/evrcwb](/audio/evrcwb).

IANA spells this type `audio/EVRCNW`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 6884 - RTP Payload Format for the Enhanced Variable Rate Narrowband-Wideband Codec (EVRC-NW)

name: audio/evrcwb
description:
EVRC-WB is the wideband member of the CDMA (Code Division Multiple Access) EVRC family. It takes the codec to a 16 kHz sampling rate, which gives noticeably clearer speech than the narrowband original. It is standardised by 3GPP2 as C.S0014-C.

RFC 5188 defines its RTP payload format and registers this media type, and in the same document updates the subtypes for EVRC-B. The narrowband original is [audio/evrc](/audio/evrc).

IANA spells this type `audio/EVRCWB`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 5188 - RTP Payload Format for the Enhanced Variable Rate Wideband Codec (EVRC-WB) and the Media Subtype Updates for EVRC-B Codec

name: audio/smv
description:
SMV (Selectable Mode Vocoder) is the speech codec 3GPP2 standardised as C.S0030 for CDMA (Code Division Multiple Access) networks. Its design goal was to let an operator choose a working point between network capacity and voice quality. Selecting one of several modes does that, rather than fixing the balance when the network is deployed.

RFC 3558 defines the RTP payload format for SMV and for the [audio/evrc](/audio/evrc) codecs, and registers this media type. Stored in the QCP file format Qualcomm defined for vocoder data, it becomes [audio/smv-qcp](/audio/smv-qcp).

IANA spells this type `audio/SMV`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 3558 - RTP Payload Format for Enhanced Variable Rate Codecs (EVRC) and Selectable Mode Vocoders (SMV)

name: audio/smv-qcp
description:
This is SMV speech stored in QCP, the RIFF-based container Qualcomm defined for vocoder data. RFC 3625 registers it along with the other codecs carried in that container.

The `.qcp` extension is shared with [audio/evrc-qcp](/audio/evrc-qcp), because the wrapper is identical and only the vocoder inside differs. The bare SMV storage format is [audio/smv](/audio/smv).

IANA spells this type `audio/SMV-QCP`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 3625 - The QCP File Format and Media Types for Speech Data
